styleBrief:
This climate tech deck demands the precision of Swiss design to match the analytical rigor of the content. Every card commits to geometric clarity and information hierarchy, using the stark contrast between dense analytical grids and dramatic single-statement compositions to mirror the urgency of climate innovation. The register is outline-based and geometric throughout—outlineBoxes for parallel market segments, stats layouts for the critical financial data, and topLineText for structured opportunity vectors. No organic shapes or decorative elements; the content's complexity provides the visual interest through grid positioning and information density.

Background alternation creates analytical rhythm: predominantly white cards with selective dark backgrounds (#1A1A1A) on 1-2 key thesis cards to create dramatic pauses in the data flow. The single accent color—a muted blue (#2B4A6B)—appears only in the stats layouts for key financial figures and in the outline boxes for sector categorization, never overwhelming the monochromatic foundation. Visual content focuses exclusively on functional elements: clean architectural diagrams of energy systems positioned alone in dedicated columns, and stark data presentations that support the analytical narrative. The behind-image treatment appears only once, on a thesis card where the H1 statement overlays an atmospheric energy infrastructure photograph.

Intentional rule-breaking occurs in the pull-quote cards, where the dramatic H1 statements break left-alignment to anchor bottom-right, creating visual tension against the predominantly left-aligned grid system. However, never use centered text, never mix decorative smart layouts, and never compromise the even column splits that give this analytical content its structural integrity. The information density varies dramatically between cards—from 300-word dense grids carrying the market analysis to single-statement breather cards that let the most critical insights breathe—but every element serves the analytical argument, never the aesthetic.
